contract: 5 — Markdown-as-you-type input rules (block and inline portions)

rows.note: Notion: `#` + space at line start.
Every level is asserted rather than asserted-by-claim.
`#`…`######` all convert.
The deepest level, so the `{1,6}` bound is proven at both ends.
Hyphen marker.

`*` converts, then serializes with the canonical `-` marker. Same class as `_soft_` → `*soft*`: a newly created node is written canonically; an untouched `* Star` already in a file is not rewritten while its block stays untouched.
`+` converts and serializes with the canonical `-` marker.
`1.` + space.
The typed start number is honoured, not reset to 1.
Bare `[]` + space, Notion's form. The space is the trigger.
Bare `[x]` + space.
`>` + space.
`---` in the document's first block creates the Properties block (MME-0090).
`***` converts and serializes as the canonical `---`.
Typing full Markdown link syntax produces a real link. Notion has no equivalent live rule; the destination is checked against the URL-safety allowlist before the mark is applied.
``` + language + space opens the fence with that language.
Applied on the closing delimiter.
Applied on the closing delimiter.
`_soft_` renders as emphasis but serializes canonically as `*soft*`; an untouched `_soft_` already in a file is never rewritten.
Backtick pair.
Contract 5 lists Notion's single `~strike~`. MME requires the CommonMark-GFM double `~~`, because that is what the persisted file means; a single `~` stays literal.

The other half of the row above: a single tilde does not convert. The backslash is MME-0120 escaping: remark-gfm parses single-tilde strikethrough by default, so unescaped literal ~gone~ would reopen struck through.
Both orderings, in the browser: the finished `**bold**` never matches the emphasis pattern, and mid-typing `**bold*` is suppressed by the word-boundary guard.
The reverse ordering.
Block rules are paragraph-only; inline rules run in any safe textblock, so formatting works inside a heading.

Notion converts this; MME does not — and MME-0120 escapes the literal so it reopens as the same literal. The criterion is 'block start or whitespace', and widening it to allow punctuation reintroduces `*italic*` swallowing `**bold**`, because mid-typing `**bold*` has `*` before the match. Recorded in BACKLOG.md as CommonMark delimiter-run flanking.
The character before the delimiter must be a block start or whitespace.
No rule fires where richTextInputContext reports an unsafe context.
